# Household Pulse Survey (HPS): agent index

The Census Bureau's online survey of US adults on how the COVID-19 pandemic and later events affected households, every one or two weeks from April 2020 (weeks 1-63, 2020-2023) and in two-week cycles in 2024 (cycles 1-9). The questionnaire was revised by phase (1, 2, 3, 3.1-3.10, 4.0-4.2). Each week or cycle is its own public use file, and its own release here.

Publisher: U.S. Census Bureau. Dataset id: `pulse`. Records follow PublicDataToolkit standard 0.1.

Terms: https://www.census.gov/about/policies/open-gov.html. LLM processing: `unknown`.

Dimensions: `wave` is the week (2020-2023) or cycle (2024).

## How the shards are organized

Every shard is the result of a filter over the records, and its header says which filter and what completeness label it supports. Each shard comes in two forms with the same variables: `.txt`, one line per variable, for scanning; and `.jsonl`, the records with corrections applied, for details. The first JSONL line is the shard's header (`{"shard": ...}`); every later line is a variable. A shard too big to read at once (about 20,000 tokens) is split into parts.

The JSONL records are compact: `availability` maps each form (or `all`) to runs of waves, `origins` gives where each field came from as `kind:source` or `rule:name@version`, and `origins.codes` is the origin the codes share (a code lists its own when they differ). Per-wave counts and the notes on origins are left out. The full records in `metadata/` are canonical; each shard header's `full_records` names the files.

Line form: `name | waves by form | scale signature | label | question text`. A run like `1972-1978` means every wave of the release in that span. `1972-1985,1987-2024 (not 1986)` means the release has a 1986 wave and the variable wasn't in it. `all 1972-1987; form A,C 1988-2024` means everyone was asked through 1987 and only forms A and C from 1988. The release's waves are: `week01`: week01; `week02`: week02; `week03`: week03; `week04`: week04; `week05`: week05; `week06`: week06; `week07`: week07; `week08`: week08; `week09`: week09; `week10`: week10; `week11`: week11; `week12`: week12; `week13`: week13; `week14`: week14; `week15`: week15; `week16`: week16; `week17`: week17; `week18`: week18; `week19`: week19; `week20`: week20; `week21`: week21; `week22`: week22; `week23`: week23; `week24`: week24; `week25`: week25; `week26`: week26; `week27`: week27; `week28`: week28; `week29`: week29; `week30`: week30; `week31`: week31; `week32`: week32; `week33`: week33; `week34`: week34; `week35`: week35; `week36`: week36; `week37`: week37; `week38`: week38; `week39`: week39; `week40`: week40; `week41`: week41; `week42`: week42; `week43`: week43; `week44`: week44; `week45`: week45; `week46`: week46; `week47`: week47; `week48`: week48; `week49`: week49; `week50`: week50; `week51`: week51; `week52`: week52; `week53`: week53; `week54`: week54; `week55`: week55; `week56`: week56; `week57`: week57; `week58`: week58; `week59`: week59; `week60`: week60; `week61`: week61; `week62`: week62; `week63`: week63; `cycle01`: cycle01; `cycle02`: cycle02; `cycle03`: cycle03; `cycle04`: cycle04; `cycle05`: cycle05; `cycle06`: cycle06; `cycle07`: cycle07; `cycle08`: cycle08; `cycle09`: cycle09. A trailing `*` on a name means a field was corrected.

`SKILL.md` says how to label an answer drawn from these files.
